I1.quote: Using an adsorption setup designed for investigating gas adsorption at high pressures by the volumetric method, isotherms of hydrogen adsorption were measured for FAS-1-05 microporous carbon adsorbent at a temperature of 77 K and pressures below 5.1 MPa
I1.location: main, p. 3 (journal p. 374), Results and Discussion, last paragraph of right column

I2.quote: Microporous FAS-1-05 and FAS-2-05 carbon adsorbents synthesized under laboratory conditions from a furaldehyde-based polymer by thermochemical synthesis were used in the experiments. ... Carbonization was carried out under an inert gas at temperatures of 1073–1123 K

I3.quote: As is seen from Fig. 3, at 77 K and 5 MPa, the adsorption reaches a value of 31 mmol/g, i.e., 6.2 wt %.
I3.location: main, p. 4 (journal p. 375), Results and Discussion, text below Fig. 3

I4.quote: Searched all text and Tables 1-3, Figs. 1-3 (no SI) for any specific surface area (BET, Langmuir, DFT, 'surface area', m2/g). None found; Table 1 gives only TVFM micropore volumes, characteristic energies and micropore half-widths.

I5.quote: Hydrogen adsorption on two samples of active carbon (FAS) produced from furaldehyde by the thermochemical synthesis method is investigated.

notes: Measured H2 uptake (volumetric, FAS-1-05, 77 K to 5.1 MPa and 293 K to 16.1 MPa, Fig. 3; both samples at 77 K, 100 Pa-100 kPa, Fig. 1 and Table 2 '9.58 / 9.78 mmol/g (experiment, 0.101 MPa, 77 K)'), so I1-I3 are met; Table 3 values are TVFM calculations, not measurements. The only porosity data are Dubinin/TVFM micropore volumes and pore half-widths (Table 1); no surface area is printed, and computing one from W0 and x0 would be our arithmetic, not a reported value, so I4 fails. The English text is the Pleiades translation of the Russian original ('Original Russian Text ... published in Kolloidnyi Zhurnal, 2008, Vol. 70, No. 3, pp. 408-412'), the same article rather than an earlier report, so duplicate_data was not applied (it would rank after no_surface_area in any case). Fig. 3 x-axis is labelled 'P, kPa' although the text gives MPa (5.1 and 16.1 MPa); the text conditions were used for I3.
